top_5_surviving_conclusions.conclusion: No VT strategy beats BH 50/50 SPY/GLD on Sharpe ratio after proper 1-day signal lag

evidence.cross_oos_wins: 0/5 (EWMA VT never beat BH in any OOS period)

top_5_surviving_conclusions.implication: VT does NOT generate alpha. The 'return enhancement' seen in prior research was a lookahead artifact. VT's value must be measured differently.

top_5_surviving_conclusions.conclusion: VT wins on CRRA utility for moderately risk-averse investors (gamma >= 5 for EWMA VT)
top_5_surviving_conclusions.implication: VT is insurance, not alpha. It's valuable for investors who strongly dislike losses (high gamma). The higher the risk aversion, the more valuable VT becomes.

top_5_surviving_conclusions.conclusion: EWMA VT is the most lag-robust strategy — weight smoothness determines survivability under implementation delay
top_5_surviving_conclusions.implication: Strategies with smoother weight paths survive implementation delays better. This explains why EWMA VT (continuous, slow-moving) retains 75.6% of its edge with 1-day lag, while Piecewise (discrete jumps) retains only 4.6%.

top_5_surviving_conclusions.conclusion: Fear DCA step function beats plain DCA by +4% per dollar invested (statistically significant)

evidence.strategy: Invest less when calm (VIX<15), normal when neutral, more when scared (VIX>25)

top_5_surviving_conclusions.implication: Simple VIX-based DCA multiplier works and is statistically robust. The step function is simplest to implement and most capital-efficient. Psychological benefit may exceed statistical improvement.

top_5_surviving_conclusions.conclusion: Fixed GARCH parameters beat rolling re-estimation for volatility targeting

evidence.key_finding: Parameter instability from rolling windows introduces noise that hurts OOS performance

top_5_surviving_conclusions.implication: Simplicity wins again. Rolling re-estimation chases structural breaks that may be noise, while fixed parameters provide stable forecasts. Consistent with EWMA VT outperforming GARCH-based VT.

top_3_lessons.lesson: Lookahead bias is the #1 threat to strategy research

evidence.inflation_factor: 4.7x (entirely from using same-day VIX for same-day return)
evidence.k689_discovery: Even paper_trading.json has same-day VIX*return lookahead
evidence.codex_caught_it: Codex review identified 3 bugs in K679 code that humans missed

top_3_lessons.rule: ALWAYS lag signals by at least 1 day. Use yesterday's VIX for today's weight. Verify by checking if Sharpe drops >50% with lag — if so, suspect lookahead.

top_3_lessons.lesson: Codex review catches what humans miss — use it systematically

evidence.k621_catch: Codex found 3 major bugs in MF2-GARCH (wrong decomposition, optimizer, data)
evidence.k679_catch: Codex identified same-day lookahead + wrong test type + percentile contamination
evidence.k689_catch: Codex-prompted investigation revealed paper trading itself has lookahead
evidence.common_pattern: All 3 catches were on code that 'looked correct' to human review
evidence.time_saved: Without K679 catch, we would have published and deployed a false strategy

top_3_lessons.rule: Every important experiment must go through Codex review before conclusions are accepted. Budget 1 review per 5-10 experiments minimum.

top_3_lessons.lesson: Simplicity wins: BH 50/50 > all active strategies on Sharpe

evidence.cross_oos_consistency: BH wins in all 5 OOS periods for EWMA VT
evidence.implication: The simplest allocation (50% SPY, 50% GLD, never touch it) is the hardest to beat
evidence.caveat: VT strategies DO win on utility for high-gamma investors (K688) — value is in tail protection, not mean return

top_3_lessons.rule: Default recommendation should be BH 50/50 unless investor has high risk aversion (gamma >= 5). Complexity must be justified by utility gain, not Sharpe improvement.

updated_strategy_recommendation.post_correction_view: VT sacrifices 0-2% CAGR in exchange for dramatic tail risk reduction. Value depends entirely on investor's risk aversion (gamma).

Maximum tail protection. CRRA utility strongly positive from gamma=10. Accept significant CAGR sacrifice.
Invest 0.5x when VIX<15, 1x when 15-25, 2-3x when VIX>25. Statistically significant improvement, simplest to implement.

limitations: This synthesis is based on the session's own experiments — meta-analysis of one's own work has inherent selection bias
The 'overturned' classification is binary — some experiments had partial value even if main conclusion was invalidated
Null results may reflect methodology limitations, not true absence of effect
Strategy recommendations assume US + Taiwan markets — generalizability untested beyond K669
CRRA utility results depend on gamma estimation, which is itself uncertain for most investors
